- If sentiment is positive (≥ 0.3) and forecast is rising sharply, reduce peak overshoot by 5–10% to avoid overcorrection.
- If sentiment is negative (≤ 0.1) and forecast is falling, avoid premature bottoming — delay downward correction by 1–2 periods.
- When sentiment swings from positive to negative, model tends to overreact — dampen forecast slope in the first 3–5 days.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 2–3% per day until convergence.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome exceeds forecast by >5% in first 5 days, assume momentum bias — adjust next 5 days downward by 1–2%.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “high-low” oscillations, forecast should be smoother — apply low-pass filter to avoid jagged peaks.
- Overshoot after spikes: if forecast peaks >15% above recent high, reduce by 10–15% in next 3 days unless sentiment confirms continuation.
